items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was the Pharoah [Sanders] to his Trane.

ctx.x: Those are all – that isn’t the working band. Those are all augmented groups.

No. Merry-Go-Round was an augmented thing. Mr. Jones was an augmented thing. But Lighthouse is the – Lighthouse is still – that’s kind of a classic among saxophone players. It captures that energy, and it captures that post-Coltrane thing. I know why Lighthouse is – I know why everybody puts it on their list. First of all, Elvin and Gene were amazing. But it’s because we, by then, had that language – whatever that language was, we had it down by then, that pentatonicy, post-Coltrane. We were the first generation…

Yeah, it’s – even at that time, in the ’70s, as soon as that record came out, a lot of the hip young saxophone players just jumped on that recorded and analyzed – that was one of those records that were like textbooks for young players. That one. Joe Henderson in Japan was like that. There were just certain records.
